metadata.title: AI Red Teaming and Evaluation

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for proactively identifying and evaluating adversarial, unsafe, or unintended behaviors in AI systems through structured testing.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: AI evaluation frameworks, adversarial testing, red teaming methodologies, and safety assessment environments.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern defining how AI systems are continuously tested against adversarial, misuse, and failure scenarios across their lifecycle.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Provides AI-specific adversarial techniques and abuse categories used as the basis for AI red teaming and evaluation scenarios.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats where adversarial input bypasses safeguards or forces the AI to violate intended use and policy.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.value: Agentic Goal Hijacking and Unsafe Planning
props.remarks: Threats where autonomous or semi-autonomous agents pursue goals in unsafe, unintended, or policy-violating ways.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats involving new or unexpected behaviors that emerge over time without explicit retraining or approval.

metadata.remarks: AI Red Teaming and Evaluation defines how AI systems are stress-tested against realistic adversarial, misuse, and failure scenarios. This pattern treats red teaming as a continuous lifecycle activity required to identify emergent behavior, unsafe autonomy, and novel attack techniques before they result in real-world harm.

components.title: Adversarial Scenario Testing
components.description: Structured testing of AI systems using known and hypothesized adversarial techniques and misuse patterns.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI systems are tested against adversarial prompts, inputs, and scenarios derived from real-world threat models.

components.title: Agent Goal Hijack Testing
components.description: Evaluation of autonomous agents to detect unsafe planning, delegation, or goal misalignment.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Agentic AI systems are evaluated for susceptibility to goal hijacking, unsafe reasoning chains, or escalation beyond authorized scope.

components.title: Post-Deployment Evaluation
components.description: Ongoing evaluation of AI systems in operation to detect emergent behaviors, drift, or degradation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI systems are periodically re-evaluated after deployment to identify new risks, behaviors, or control erosion.
